summary: A river valley between Cleveland and Akron, protected as forests, farms, waterfalls and the towpath of the Ohio & Erie Canal. The only national park that began as a national recreation area, and one of the most visited.
story: The Cuyahoga River winds south to north through a valley cut by glacial meltwater, its sides falling away in ravines and waterfalls. Brandywine Falls drops sixty-five feet over layered shale and sandstone; at the Ledges, blocks of the Sharon Conglomerate stand in mossy cliffs above the forest.

Much of the valley was farmed or built on, and it is recovering in plain sight. The Beaver Marsh on the Towpath Trail was an auto junkyard until beavers returned and flooded it; great blue herons nest in colonies, and bald eagles hunt over the river again.

The Hopewell people built mounds here around two thousand years ago, and many nations, including the Lenape, later lived in or passed through the valley. The Ohio & Erie Canal opened between Cleveland and Akron in 1827 and ran until the great flood of 1913; its towpath is now a trail. Pollution on the lower Cuyahoga was so bad that the river caught fire in Cleveland in 1969, a moment that helped spur national environmental law.

Congress set the valley aside as a national recreation area in 1974 and made it a national park in 2000. Within its boundaries are towns, county parks, farms and a scenic railroad, and there is no entrance fee.

sights.name: Brandywine Falls
sights.note: A sixty-five-foot waterfall seen from a boardwalk, the park's best-known view.

sights.name: The Ledges
sights.note: Sandstone cliffs and cool, mossy passages, with a west-facing overlook for sunset.

sights.name: Beaver Marsh
sights.note: A former junkyard turned wetland on the Towpath Trail, alive with beavers, herons and turtles.

sights.name: Everett Covered Bridge
sights.note: A reconstructed nineteenth-century covered bridge over Furnace Run.

sights.name: Towpath Trail at Lock 29
sights.note: The canal towpath at the village of Peninsula, for walking or cycling along the river.

sights.name: Boston Mill
sights.note: A stop on the scenic railroad, beside the park's main visitor center.

entrances: No single entrance: roads cross the valley between Cleveland and Akron. Start at Boston Mill Visitor Center in Peninsula
The Cuyahoga Valley Scenic Railroad runs the length of the park
lodging: The Stanford House, a historic farmhouse available to rent, and inns and towns nearby
seasonalClosures: Lake-effect snow from Lake Erie can arrive quickly in winter; autumn colour usually peaks in mid-October

chronology.text: The Ohio & Erie Canal opens between Cleveland and Akron.
A great flood ends the canal's working life.
A fire on the polluted Cuyahoga River in Cleveland draws national attention.
Cuyahoga Valley National Recreation Area is established.
The recreation area is redesignated a national park.

safety: The Towpath Trail is shared by walkers and cyclists; keep right and listen for bells.
Ledges and gorge edges are slick when wet or icy. Stay on trails.
regulations: There is no entrance fee; some railroad and private attractions charge their own.
Drones may not be launched, landed or flown in the park.
